chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Failing a Wall Street physical, high blood pressure, and a hospital stay in England
summary: He failed a Wall Street job physical, discusses hereditary high blood pressure, and a ten-day hospital stay in England before a Bern gig.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yes. I went down to Wall Street to apply for that job because Dickie Wells had told me. But I was in such bad shape I didn't even pass the physical. Because the guy, you see, this is my, the fourth time I'd been operated on both of these hernias once before and not knowing it, maybe I'd started playing again too soon and they both reoccurred and I didn't know it. When I went down there the doctor said, he felt me and he says, you've got to go back to the doctor's because those things have reoccurred. And blood pressure was high.
Oh I always had the high blood pressure.
For years now, I don't know how long, I don't know when it started, but I think, they say that's hereditary. My father had it, I know that.
Yes, that's like my father had low blood pressure.

Oh, my mother had it. Yes, both of them. My father had high blood pressure and my mother had high blood pressure. So I had a little trouble with that in England. I was in the hospital for ten days in England.
Yes I remember hearing, having alarming reports.

Yes, yes. Well, I actually, they could have let me out after the second day but they kept me there to try to figure out why. And they gave me all kinds of tests and they still couldn't find out why. They gave me a liver test and ex-rays and they still never found out.
Well that didn't cost anything did it?
No. They let me out just in time to go to Bern, Switzerland and I got to Bern, Switzerland.
By that time you felt better I guess, eh?

Laying in the hospital just doing nothing, I wasn't bleeding or anything. I was just laying there waiting for dinner time to come. But it was a good rest, you see, so when I got out I flew right to Bern, Switzerland and played at the Chikita Club.

Then I went from Bern to Belgium. From Belgium back to France and from France back home. But I've had, my pressure has been high for years and years and years ago and I don't know when it first started. But anyway, it's normal now but I have to keep it that way, but if I don't do anything it would right back up.
Well what do you............(UNABLE TO HEAR END OF SENTENCE).
